source: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars composite parameters (default rows)

provenance.query: select pl_name,pl_orbper,pl_orbpererr1,pl_orbpererr2,pl_tranmid,pl_tranmid_systemref,pl_trandur,pl_bmassj,pl_radj,st_mass from pscomppars where pl_name in ('Kepler-9 b','Kepler-9 c','Kepler-36 b','Kepler-36 c','Kepler-20 b','Kepler-20 c') and default_flag=1
provenance.independence: Values are the archive's published composite parameters retrieved live from the NASA Exoplanet Archive and frozen here for offline deterministic tests. They are not generated by this repository.
provenance.notes: Discovery-era values differ from the current archive composites: Holman et al. (2010, Science, 330, 51, doi:10.1126/science.1195778; ADS 2010Sci...330...51H) report Kepler-9 b P = 19.243158 d and Kepler-9 c P = 38.90861 d; Carter et al. (2012, Science, 337, 556) report Kepler-36 b P = 13.83989 d and Kepler-36 c P = 16.23855 d. The long-baseline composite parameters retained here are the authoritative current archive values.

kepler-36.resonance: near 7:6 high-order resonance (7:6 is outside the first-order factor set and must not be promoted)

kepler-20.resonance: none: period ratio ~2.9367 is far from every first-order factor
